"(A) YOUR LORDSHIPS may be pleased to issue a writ of mandamus and/or any other appropriate writ, order or NEUTRAL CITATION C/SCA/10283/2024 ORDER DATED: 08/08/2024 undefined directions quashing setting and aside the impugned action of temporary acquisition of the land in question having Block No.1116/1,
admeasuring 00-50-74 [Hec.RA.Sq.Mts], situated at Village: Padra (Kasba),
Tal:Padra, Dist: Vadodara, temporarily acquired by respondent no.3 O.N.G.C. Corp.

and further be pleased to issue directions upon respondent no.3 to release the land in question in its original state in favour of the petitioners; ALTERNATIVELY (B) YOUR LORDSHIPS maybe pleased to issue a writ of mandamus and/or any other appropriate writ, order or directions upon the respondent no.3 Corporation to modify and increase the periodic compensation at the rate of 15%
per annum of the prevailing market value of the land in question having Block No.1116/1,
admeasuring 00-50-74 [Hec.RA.Sq.Mts], situated at Village: Padra (Kasba), Tal:
Padra, Dist: Vadodara, with effect from 06.07.2015 along with arrears at rate of interest of 12% per annum till the date of realisation of the land in question;
(C) During the pendency and final disposal of the present petition YOUR LORDSHIPS maybe pleased to direct the respondent no.3 Corporation to modify and increase the periodic compensation at the rate of 15% per annum of the prevailing market value of the land in question having Block No.1116/1, admeasuring 00-50-74 [Hec.RA.Sq.Mts], situated at Village: Padra (Kasba), Tal: Padra, Dist: Vadodara, with effect from 06.07.2015 along with arrears at rate of interest of 12% per annum till the date of realisation of the land in question;"
NEUTRAL CITATION C/SCA/10283/2024 ORDER DATED: 08/08/2024 undefined [3] The petitioners herein are the original owners of the land in question and the dispute revolves around the possession of the land with the Respondent - ONGC.

It is stated in the writ petition that the Respondent - ONGC have temporarily acquired the land in question by executing an Agreement dated 05.04.1989, for an area of 5074 sq.mts, on the premise that they needed the land in question for temporary use and in case it was found to be useful, proceedings for permanent acquisition of the land in question would be initiated under the Land Acquisition Act, 1894.
[4] From the averments made in the affidavit filed on behalf of the Respondent - ONGC, it is evident that the land acquisition proceedings were initiated in the year 1992 and later in 2018 - 2019 and 2020, but the said proceeding was not brought to its logical end.
From the stage of proposal for acquisition of land, the matter had not been proceeded further.
[5] The ONGC, however, continued in possession of the land in question and an Agreement dated 08.02.2002 had been signed by the land owners with the Authorities of ONGC.

A perusal of the said Agreement at Page '65 / 68 A' of the Hitesh Maganbhai Patel vs State Of Gujarat on 8 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/55570399/

sentences.text: Paper-book indicates that the annual rent of the land in question at the rate of Rs.380/- per acre, until the acquisition NEUTRAL CITATION C/SCA/10283/2024 ORDER DATED: 08/08/2024 undefined process was completed or the Corporation releases the land, was fixed.

[6] It may further be noted that that the clauses of Agreement stated that the land owners would not be entitled for making any claim for compensation beyond the agreed term and the Agreement will remain in effect until the land acquisition process was completed or the land was released by the Corporation.

Similar is the position about the Agreement dated 15.06.2008, a copy of which is appended at Page '68/C'.
[7] However, it seems that with the advent of the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013, the proceedings for acquisition was not taken further, after the enforcement of the said Act with effect from 01.01.2014.

entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: [8] The instant petition raising grievances with regard to continuance of ONGC over the land in question has been filed in the month of June 2024 with the primary relief that the ONGC be directed to handover vacant and peaceful possession of the land in question as they cannot continue to acquire the land on the premise of temporary acquisition with the assurance to the land owners to pay compensation after permanent acquisition.
NEUTRAL CITATION C/SCA/10283/2024 ORDER DATED: 08/08/2024 undefined

[9] As noted hereinbefore, each time, ONGC had persuaded the land owners to allow it to retain possession of the land in question on the premise that the land in question would be permanently acquired and the arrangement through the agreement was till conclusion of the acquisition proceedings.

[10] Be that as it may, in the affidavit dated 29.07.2024 filed by the General Manager (Production), ONGC, it is sought to be stated that on a techno - economic analysis of the subject land, taking into account all the acquisition cause of the total land depleting production profile of the existing well No.11, the ONGC has decided to return the land in question to the petitioners by restoring it to its original position.

[11] It is, thus, submitted that the competent authority of the ONGC has decided not to acquire the land in question in line with the prayer made by the petitioner and the proceedings for restoration of the land in question would be undertaken as per the standard operating procedure to handover the vacant possession of the land in question to the land owners within the period of six months.

[12] On these submissions of the ONGC, in Rejoinder, NEUTRAL CITATION C/SCA/10283/2024 ORDER DATED: 08/08/2024 undefined the learned counsel for Hitesh Maganbhai Patel vs State Of Gujarat on 8 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/55570399/

sentences.text: the petitioner has invited attention of this Court to Section 36 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 to submit that at the time of restoration of the land in question, the persons interested would be required to be compensated for the damages caused to the land in question, if restoration is not completed in the manner that the land in question becomes fertile for agricultural operations as per the local conditions.

[13] The submission is that it is the duty and responsibility of the ONGC to ensure that the restoration of the land in question to its original possession, meaning thereby, the restored land should be fit for agricultural operations for which it was being used at the time of acquisition by ONGC vide Agreement dated 05.04.1989.

Any situation where the land in question becomes unfit for agricultural operations as per the local conditions, the land holders would have to be compensated for the damages caused to them by the Collector, who is required to assess the same.
[14] Taking note of the above, we find it fit and proper to dispose of the present petition with the directions as follows:
1. The Respondent - ONGC shall complete the process of NEUTRAL CITATION C/SCA/10283/2024 ORDER DATED: 08/08/2024 undefined restoration of the land in question, already initiated, to its original status as per the standard operating procedure and ensure that the land becomes useful for the agricultural operations, as per the local conditions.
2.
The exercise of restoration of the land in question by providing vacant and peaceful possession of the same to the land holders shall be completed within the period of six months.

3. However, before handing over possession of the land in question to the petitioner,
an evaluation of the conditions of the restored land shall be made by the Collector,
Vadodara by engaging experts so as to ensure that the fertility of the land in question for agricultural operations is restored.
4. In the exercise for assessment of the status of the restored land, both the land owners and representatives of ONGC shall be allowed to participate.

5. In case the land is found in deficient in any aspect after restoration, the Collector shall be required to take an independent decision for awarding damages to the land holders or any other direction as he may deem fit in the facts and circumstances before him.
NEUTRAL CITATION C/SCA/10283/2024 ORDER DATED: 08/08/2024 undefined 6.
In the meantime, the rent fixed by the parties, due if any, shall be paid by the ONGC.
